reason: Both conversations correctly identified an earth fault, flagged the heater element as the likely culprit on heated-wash-only trips, told him to stop resetting the RCD and unplug, and escalated to an engineer; neither asked which device trips, about other circuits, or for the full model number. Conversation 2 lost ground by instructing a homeowner with no meter and no comfort with wiring to remove the rear panel, disconnect the element wires and run a multimeter continuity test, which is both unsuited to this user and technically the wrong test (a cold continuity check will not reliably reveal insulation breakdown that only appears when hot; an insulation tester is needed). Conversation 1 went straight to 'engineer to insulation-test and replace element', hedged appropriately with 'strongly points to', and avoided the DIY detour, though its second safety banner about burning smells was boilerplate that did not match what he had just said. Conversation 2's recovery in its final turn was sound, but Conversation 1 reached the right outcome more safely and efficiently.
